sector: Communication Services / SMB SaaS (former Dex Media yellow-pages)
drawdown_context: THRY is the post-bankruptcy Dex Media / YP yellow-pages business that re-IPO'd in 2020 and is pivoting to a SaaS 'business management' platform (Thryv Platform + Keap Acquisition Oct 2024). The 10-K (filed 2025-02-27) discloses FY24 net loss of $74.2M, $83.1M goodwill impairment (3rd consecutive year: $83.1M / $268.8M / $102.2M = $454M cumulative), Marketing Services revenue down 26.4% YoY (still 58.3% of consolidated revenue, with management announcing in 2024 it will TERMINATE Marketing Services by end of 2028), and a new $350M senior-secured Term Loan at SOFR+6.75% (~12% all-in) with 40% held by a 5%+ related-party shareholder. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01, 14 days pre-cutoff) shows the trajectory accelerated: Marketing Services revenue down 55.9% YoY (vs FY24's -26.4%), SaaS ARPU down 9% YoY, Segment Adjusted EBITDA collapsed -61% YoY from $54.1M to $20.9M, net loss $9.6M (vs Q1 2024 net income $8.4M), cash on hand $11.0M against $26.3M of current Term Loan principal due. Forward return -72.7% confirms the SaaS-pivot narrative was not adequate cover for the legacy MS cash-engine collapsing faster than SaaS could scale.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Audit Report (Grant Thornton LLP, 2/27/2025): unqualified opinion. 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2022.' No going-concern paragraph, no substantial-doubt language. Critical Audit Matter is the defined-benefit pension obligation actuarial assumptions (Note: pensions are frozen, PBO $320M vs plan assets $280M = $40M underfunded).
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_local on 10-K AND most-recent pre-cutoff 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01); Mode B: auditor change in 2022 (when did they replace prior firm? Why?). What is the CAM, and does it foreshadow the FY25 problem area?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: 0 hits on 'substantial doubt', 2 hits on 'going concern' (both in risk-factor boilerplate, not auditor opinion). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01): also NO going-concern language despite -61% EBITDA collapse. Auditor: Grant Thornton (not Big 4 — tier 2), tenure only 3 years (since 2022). Prior auditor was likely Ernst & Young (changed 2022 — coincides with Vivial close and the year before $268.8M goodwill impairment).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor profile is weaker than implied by the clean opinion: Grant Thornton replaced prior firm in 2022 (the year Vivial closed and the year before $268.8M goodwill impairment). For a $700M-asset company with $284M of secured debt at SOFR+6.75%, tier-2 auditor + 3-year tenure + CAM on pension (not goodwill, despite three straight years of MS impairments) is a thin signal. Mode B: the CAM should have been on Marketing Services goodwill recoverability, not pensions — auditor avoided the harder question.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'We made the strategic decision to terminate our Marketing Services solutions by the end of 2028 and accelerate the conversion of Marketing Services clients to our Thryv SaaS offerings.' 'During 2024, 58.3% of our revenue was derived from our Marketing Services offerings.' FY24 MS revenue -26.4% YoY; FY24 SaaS revenue grew $79.8M (Keap contributed ~$13.4M from Oct'24 close).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on revenue mix + claim_evolution (10-K vs Q1 2025 10-Q); Mode B: is the SaaS growth organic, Keap-driven, or just MS-conversion (revenue migration without net new dollars)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q: Marketing Services revenue -55.9% YoY ($159.3M -> $70.2M), more than double the FY24 -26.4% pace. SaaS revenue +49.5% YoY ($74.3M -> $111.1M) — BUT $18.9M of that growth is Keap (inorganic), and $11.3M is MS->SaaS conversion (revenue migration, not new dollars). Net organic SaaS growth = $36.8M - $18.9M Keap - $11.3M conversion = ~$6.6M, or ~9% organic vs the headline 49.5%. Total revenue: $233.6M -> $181.4M = -22.4% consolidated revenue decline in a single quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The SaaS-pivot narrative collapses under decomposition: headline 49.5% SaaS growth is ~80% inorganic/migration, with only ~9% organic SaaS growth — far below the ~25-30% needed to outpace the 56% MS collapse. The 10-K framed termination of MS as a strategic choice; the Q1 10-Q reveals MS revenue is collapsing FASTER than the SaaS pivot can absorb. Mode B claim evolution dispositive: in 90 days the MS decline pace more than doubled while SaaS organic growth was modest.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 10: '$350.0 million [New Term Loan Facility], of which 40.0% was held by a related party who was an equity holder of the Company as of May 1, 2024. The Company defines a related party as any shareholder owning more than 5% of the Company's voting securities.' Interest: SOFR + 6.75% (SOFR loans) or base rate + 5.75%. Matures May 1, 2029. Mandatory amortization $52.5M/yr first two years.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on debt structure; Mode B: related-party financing at SOFR+6.75% (~12% all-in) when investment-grade SMB SaaS peers (HUBS, BILL) are unlevered or sub-6% — what does the related-party participation imply about market access?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Term Loan all-in coupon ~SOFR(~5.3%) + 6.75% = ~12% — distressed pricing for a $700M company. Related-party 40% = $140M held by a 5%+ shareholder, who under SEC rules is captured but not named in this disclosure (likely Mudrick Capital or other DE post-restructuring holder from the 2016 Chapter 11). FY24 interest expense $46.8M (of which $10.3M was to related party). Q1 2025 interest expense $9.1M with $3.0M to related party. Total debt $284.3M at Dec'24 against $16.3M cash = 17.4x debt-to-cash; debt/Adjusted EBITDA (with $24.8M pension remeasurement gain stripped) = $284M / $137M = 2.07x — within the 3.0x covenant but tight on quality of EBITDA.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A profitable SaaS company does not borrow at SOFR+6.75% with 40% of paper held by a related-party holder. The Term Loan terms and counterparty mix are the credit market's verdict: third-party institutional lenders would not fund the full amount at that spread, requiring the related-party post-restructuring holder to backstop 40%. Mode B: this is the structural fingerprint of distressed-debt-as-DIP-replacement, not growth capital. The 'in compliance with covenants' language masks that the covenant package itself (3.0x Total Net Leverage + SaaS Revenue minimum) is a distressed covenant set, not a typical SaaS investment-grade structure.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Key Business Metrics: 'ARPU (Monthly) Marketing Services $133 [FY24] $158 [FY23] $178 [FY22]; SaaS $330 [FY24] $372 [FY23] $369 [FY22].' MS ARPU -16% YoY 2024 vs -11% YoY 2023. SaaS ARPU -11% YoY 2024 vs +1% YoY 2023. 'The decrease in SaaS ARPU during the year ended December 31, 2024 primarily resulted from our strategic decision to accelerate the conversion of clients from digital Marketing Services solutions to our SaaS offerings at no additional base cost.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on ARPU evolution + claim_evolution; Mode B: SaaS ARPU declining YoY is the OPPOSITE of what a 'SaaS transformation' should produce — is management actually destroying SaaS quality by force-migrating low-payers?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q: MS ARPU $111 vs $145 prior-year Q1 (-23% YoY, accelerating from FY24's -16%). SaaS ARPU $335 vs $369 prior-year Q1 (-9% YoY). Two-year stack on SaaS ARPU: $369 -> $335 = -9% in 24 months on the segment management is supposedly pivoting INTO. As of Mar'25, approximately 34,000 converted MS clients remain active SaaS — these clients pay no incremental base cost, structurally depressing blended ARPU as the mix shifts.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A genuine SaaS transformation should show flat-to-rising ARPU as customers upsell. Thryv's SaaS ARPU is declining because the 'SaaS clients' added are former Marketing Services clients moved over at no incremental cost — a definitional sleight that boosts the SaaS client count (numerator) and SaaS revenue (mix benefit) while degrading SaaS unit economics. Mode B: 'SaaS NRR' and seat-growth disclosures are CONSPICUOUSLY ABSENT from the 10-K. A real SaaS company would disclose net revenue retention; THRY discloses only blended ARPU, which is being structurally diluted by the conversion strategy.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Our impairment tests resulted in non-cash impairments of our goodwill of $83.1 million, $268.8 million and $102.2 million during the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively, to reduce goodwill in our Thryv Marketing Services reporting unit. The impairment charge during the year ended December 31, 2024 was primarily driven by the Company's strategic decision during the third quarter of 2024 to terminate its Marketing Services solutions by the end of 2028.' Balance: Goodwill at Dec'24 = $253.3M (all in Thryv SaaS reporting unit; Marketing Services goodwill is now $0).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + Mode B: with $454M of cumulative MS goodwill impairment + Keap $34.4M of new goodwill in SaaS unit, is the remaining $253M SaaS goodwill recoverable given the SaaS unit's $54.1M -> $20.9M EBITDA drop in Q1?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three consecutive years of impairments — $102.2M (2022) + $268.8M (2023) + $83.1M (2024) = $454.1M cumulative writedowns of Marketing Services goodwill. MS goodwill is now zero. ALL $253.3M of remaining goodwill is in the SaaS reporting unit (including $34.4M from Keap). SaaS segment Q1 2025 Adjusted EBITDA $10.8M (annualized $43M) against $253M of carried goodwill = 5.9x EV/EBITDA on goodwill alone, before assigning any value to operating assets — i.e. SaaS unit must triple to make goodwill recoverable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Pattern of serial impairments is a 'one more year' tell — 2022, 2023, 2024 each saw 'final' impairment of MS goodwill before the next round. With MS now zeroed, the remaining $253M is concentrated in a SaaS unit whose Q1 2025 organic growth is ~9% (not 49.5%) and whose EBITDA more than tripled YoY only because the comparison base was tiny ($3.4M -> $10.8M). Mode B: Keap's $34.4M goodwill was booked Oct 2024 against $13.4M of revenue contribution in 11 weeks — implied multiple is high. Next impairment cycle is likely SaaS goodwill — the auditor's CAM on pensions (not goodwill) suggests they have not flagged this.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note: 'No single client accounted for more than 5% of the Company's outstanding accounts receivable as of December 31, 2024 or 2023.' 'The Company's top ten directories, as measured by revenue, accounted for approximately 2% of total revenue. No single directory or client accounted for more than 1% of the Company's revenue for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022.' 'Google in particular is the most significant source of traffic to our IYPs and to our clients' websites.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on customer + counterparty concentration; Mode B: SMB SaaS doesn't have customer concentration but typically has CHANNEL concentration — what is the Google/Yelp/Facebook search-traffic dependency?
rfm_tuples.M_value: No client concentration risk (diversified SMB base, ~400K+ clients). HOWEVER: search/traffic dependency on Google is explicitly acknowledged ('most significant source of traffic to our IYPs and to our clients' websites'). Competition disclosure: 'Google, Yelp and Facebook' — i.e., THRY's MS revenue base is being eaten by the same platforms it depends on for traffic. No specific Google revenue-share disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Customer concentration claim is supported (diversified SMB base). Mode A passes. Mode B: the channel-concentration / Google-as-frenemy structural exposure is disclosed but not quantified — typical for SMB advertising business, not specific to THRY misrepresentation.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Adjusted EBITDA $162,431 [FY24] vs $187,515 [FY23], 19.7% vs 20.4% of revenue.' Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation adds back: D&A $51.4M, interest expense $46.8M, taxes $8.2M, stock comp $25.4M, restructuring/integration $14.3M, OTHER COMPONENTS OF NET PERIODIC PENSION BENEFIT $(24.8M), other $2.0M.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on EBITDA quality; Mode B: pension remeasurement gain of $24.8M is non-cash AND non-operating — is the 'Adjusted EBITDA' inflated by stripping in a gain that doesn't recur?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Net periodic pension benefit included a $31.1M REMEASUREMENT GAIN in FY24 (driven by discount-rate increase) — this is reflected in the $24.8M net pension credit added back to Adjusted EBITDA. If pension remeasurement gain is excluded (proper treatment per non-GAAP best practices), Adjusted EBITDA FY24 = $162.4M - $24.8M pension benefit + ~0 normalized pension = ~$137.6M. FY23 had only $2.7M pension benefit. Apples-to-apples FY24 vs FY23 with normalized pension: $137.6M vs ~$184.8M = -25.5% Adjusted EBITDA decline (vs the reported -13.4%). Q1 2025 reconciliation shows pension cost OF $0.8M (positive cost, not benefit) — the FY24 tailwind is reversing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's headline Adjusted EBITDA understates operating deterioration by stripping in a $24.8M non-cash pension remeasurement gain that is a balance-sheet phenomenon, not operating income. Properly normalized, the FY24 EBITDA decline is closer to 25%, not the 13% headline. Q1 2025 confirms: pension credit reversed to a cost, and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation no longer benefits from this tailwind. Mode B: classic 'non-GAAP add-back creep' tell — when a one-time gain helps, it's included; when one-time gains hurt, they're excluded.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'On October 29, 2024 ... we closed an underwritten public offering of 5,715,000 shares of common stock, generating proceeds of $76.8 million (after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions) and borrowed $5.5 million under our New ABL Facility.' Plus Nov 12, 2024 over-allotment of 857,250 shares for $11.5M. Total: 6.57M shares issued to finance ~$77M Keap purchase. 'Board authorized a new share repurchase program ... up to $40 million in shares ... through April 30, 2029.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on capital allocation + insider_vs_calendar around equity issuance and buyback authorization; Mode B: simultaneously issuing equity (Oct'24) and authorizing buyback (Apr'24, kept open) is asymmetric.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 39 Form 4 filings between Aug 2024 and May 2025 (pre-cutoff). Equity issued at ~$13.43/share net. Stock cutoff price was $14.56 (May 15 2025) — modestly above issuance. Share count went from 60.8M (FY21) to 70.6M shares issued + 43.0M outstanding at Dec'24 (substantial treasury). Buyback program $40M authorized April 2024; the 10-K's narrative implies buybacks were paused. Mode B: management chose Keap acquisition financing via dilutive equity issuance (~6.6M shares at ~$13) over debt — implies even THRY mgmt viewed debt market as too expensive at SOFR+6.75%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Equity issuance to fund Keap, while a $40M buyback program is authorized in parallel and a related-party holds 40% of the term loan, is a fragmented capital structure that benefits the related-party lender (paid 12% coupon) while diluting common shareholders. Mode B: insider Form 4s are dominated by award (A) and forfeit-to-cover (F) codes typical of SBC vesting; no large open-market purchases by management around the Keap close or 10-K filing — i.e. insiders did not signal conviction at issuance prices.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Balance Sheet: 'Cash and cash equivalents $16.3M [Dec'24]'. Current portion of Term Loan $7.875M; Current portion of Term Loan, related party $5.25M. Total current Term Loan principal $13.1M; mandatory amortization $52.5M/year first two years means $39.4M will become current within 12 months. Q1 2025 10-Q: Cash $11.0M.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on liquidity adequacy; Mode B: $11M cash against $52.5M annual mandatory amortization + $46M annual interest + pension cash contributions = ~$110M of fixed cash obligations against ~$162M of (overstated) Adjusted EBITDA.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dec'24 cash $16.3M; Mar'25 cash $11.0M (-32% in one quarter). ABL Facility ($85M total capacity, $23.9M drawn = $61M undrawn) is the primary liquidity buffer. Normalized fixed-charge coverage: ($137.6M normalized EBITDA - $46.8M interest - $52.5M amortization) = ~$38M of free cash before working capital, capex, integration costs. Keap integration costs and restructuring (legacy MS wind-down through 2028) will consume that buffer. The ABL is the lifeline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cash position is critically thin: $11M against $52.5M of mandatory annual term loan amortization and $46M interest expense. The 10-K's 'we believe ... will be sufficient to meet our liquidity requirements ... for the next 12 months' relies entirely on the ABL undraws ($61M). With MS revenue collapsing 56% YoY in Q1 and SaaS EBITDA at $10.8M/qtr, the ABL has 12-18 months of runway absent re-acceleration. Mode B: the absence of any near-cutoff cap raise, secondary offering, or convertible (post-Keap dilution) suggests management has limited equity-issuance optionality at current prices.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 2 Acquisitions history: YP Holdings (2017), Vivial (Jan 2022), Yellow New Zealand (Apr 2023), Sensis Australia, Keap (Oct 2024). Roll-up cadence: ~one acquisition every 12-18 months over the past 5 years. 10-K Risk Factor: 'business uncertainties as a result of the Keap Acquisition; the potential impact of write-downs or write-offs and impairment or other charges from the Keap Acquisition; significant transaction costs in connection with the Keap Acquisition.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on roll-up integration history + Mode B: what is the track record of acquired businesses' GAAP performance vs deal economics? Vivial booked a 'bargain purchase gain' in 2022 — what was the realized vs deal-model performance?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Vivial 2022 acquisition recorded a bargain purchase GAIN — i.e. acquired assets were marked above purchase price, generating non-cash GAAP income. Vivial then became part of Marketing Services which was impaired by $268.8M in 2023 (a year later) and $83.1M in 2024 (two years later). Yellow New Zealand (Apr 2023): no separate disclosure of integration outcome; rolled into international MS which is in the segment management decided to terminate. Keap (Oct 2024) contributed $13.4M revenue and $5.3M net LOSS in its first 11 weeks — losing money out of the gate. 10-K's own risk factor lists Keap integration risks as the leading 'Risks Related to the Keap Acquisition.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The roll-up pattern is consistent with private-equity playbook from the 2016 Chapter 11 reorg sponsors: acquire SMB assets at low multiples, book bargain-purchase gains, then impair the goodwill over the next 2-3 years. Vivial -> 2023 impairment is the proof point. Keap fits the pattern (already loss-making in stub period, $34.4M goodwill against $5.3M of 11-week losses). Mode B: the 10-K's silence on integration KPIs from prior deals (Vivial revenue retention, Yellow NZ ARPU trends) is itself the implied-verification signal — successful roll-ups disclose unit-level success metrics; THRY discloses only consolidated segments that get later impaired.

summary: Thryv is a post-bankruptcy Dex Media yellow-pages roll-up dressed up as an SMB SaaS transformation. The 10-K is technically clean (no going-concern, tier-2 auditor Grant Thornton's unqualified opinion) but the implied-verification signals are uniformly negative and ALL get worse in the Q1 2025 10-Q filed 14 days before cutoff. Mode A: claims like 'no customer concentration' and 'in compliance with covenants' verify. Mode B (dispositive): (1) MS revenue decline more than DOUBLED from -26% in FY24 to -56% in Q1 2025 while SaaS organic growth is only ~9% (the rest is Keap inorganic + MS->SaaS conversion); (2) Segment Adjusted EBITDA collapsed 61% YoY in Q1 2025 with MS segment down 80%; (3) Term Loan at SOFR+6.75% (~12% all-in) with 40% held by a related-party 5%+ shareholder = distress pricing requiring insider backstop; (4) SaaS ARPU declining -9% in 24 months — the opposite of a healthy SaaS transformation; (5) Three consecutive years of MS goodwill impairment ($454M cumulative) with the same pattern likely to repeat on remaining $253M SaaS goodwill; (6) Cash burned from $16M to $11M in one quarter against $52.5M annual mandatory amortization; (7) Adjusted EBITDA inflated by $24.8M non-cash pension remeasurement gain — normalized YoY decline is -25% not -13%; (8) Roll-up history of bargain-purchase gains followed by impairments (Vivial 2022 -> impaired 2023+2024) is being repeated with Keap. The framework should flag THRY as high-severity SHORT-tier: the SaaS-pivot narrative is empirically failing in Q1 10-Q, and management is obscuring the slope of deterioration via non-GAAP add-backs, segment-mix accounting, and forced MS->SaaS conversions that dilute SaaS unit economics.
